newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Costello says Budget changes cost A$400 mln.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Costello says Budget changes cost A$400 mln.

text.p: Australian Treasurer Peter Costello said changes imposed on a budget bill by the Senate on Tuesday would cost about A$400 million over the coming four fiscal years, to June 2000.

"In total, these amendments together with the direct costs arising from the defeat of the government's proposal on carer's pension, widow's allowance, child disability allowance, special benefit, maternity allowance, additional family payment, health care cards and parenting allowance will total A$400 million, requiring the government to borrow this sum to pay the benefits," Costello said in a statement.
The bill was supposed to save A$550 million in that period.
Costello itemised these four-year costs of the amendments:
-- The defeat of a government plan to exclude immigrants from various social security payments, apart from unemployment benefits: A$227 million.
-- The dilution of a plan to exclude immigrants from unemployment benefits for two years, the Senate insisting that immigrants be unrestricted on a similar payment: A$107 million.
-- Other impacts, including delays in implementation: $78 million.
The bill was the first major element of the government's deficit-slashing budget to come before the Senate.
The upper house of parliament is scheduled over the next two weeks to deal with most other bills in the budget programme, which aimed to save A$7.2 billion in the fiscal year to June 1998.
